Subject: Isolation playbook & POC onboarding for MedSuite — next steps

Hi Matt —

Great conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on tenancy and isolation expectations before we scope the POC: 

1) High-level ask from MedSuite: isolation guarantees for customer work, predictable p95 latency <= 120ms for inference on baseline models, and clear blast-radius boundaries for other tenants.

2) Redwood options we discussed:
   - Hosted API (multi-tenant): fastest to start; we recommend prefix/KV caching and dedicated routing if you need lower tail latency.
   - Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools): predictable throughput + soft isolation via reserved pools; good fit if you need SLA-backed latency and commit-oriented pricing.
   - Private VPC / on-prem: full tenancy control, network isolation, KMS integration, longer procurement.

3) Noisy-neighbor mitigation we can provide during POC: continuous batching profile tuning, request-class routing, and an isolation playbook for escalation (attached).

4) Next steps (proposed):
   - You share a short list of representative traffic patterns (inference qps, modal payload sizes) — we can use the attached POC worksheet to capture this.
   - We provision a low-friction POC: 2 weeks using Dedicated capacity with a safety fallback to Hosted in case load spikes.
   - Security checklist + sample SLA language to go to procurement (cc Ben for legal hooks).

Attachments: [Attachment: isolation-playbook.pdf (12 KB)], [Attachment: redwood-poc-worksheet.xlsx (9 KB)]

Let us know if that aligns and if legal should be looped in now. Happy to schedule a 30-min technical kickoff tomorrow if convenient.

Thanks,

- Can you confirm whether Dedicated gives us hardware-level isolation or just pool reservation? Our compliance team is asking specifically about "no cross-VM inference" guarantees.

Matt — thanks for the clear questions. A few targeted answers to help procurement and compliance decide: 

- Dedicated capacity is reservation of GPU pools (not single-tenant VMs by default). It provides strong tenant isolation at the scheduling and network levels (no tenant shares the same process space), but it is not the same as physically air-gapped single-tenant hardware. For single-tenant physical isolation we recommend Private VPC or on-prem deployment.

- Latency breakdown: in our typical Dedicated deployments with standard nv4-like instances (FP16 quantized models), inference accounts for ~60–75% of the p95; network + serialization is the remainder. With the optimizations we discussed (continuous batching tuned for your qps profile, KV prefix caching for hot prompts) it's realistic to hit p95 <= 120ms for small/medium tokens on the models you demoed. We will provide a sample histogram from a similar customer during the kickoff.

- Audit logs: Dedicated includes request logs and metadata; we offer field-level redaction and short-term retention in Dedicated. Private gives you longer retention windows and direct KMS/HSM control. For the POC, we can enable per-request tracing and export samples to an S3 bucket (or your object storage) for the two-week window.

POC proposal (technical):
- Duration: 2 weeks
- Mode: Dedicated capacity with burst fallback to Hosted (policy-based)
- Success criteria: sustained p95 <= 120ms at your target qps, no >1% error rate on inference calls, and request logs available for audit sampling

I'll put together a short runbook and capacity estimate once you fill the POC worksheet. Olga — happy to run the kickoff; suggest Wed 31 Aug 10:00 PT.

Cheers,
